details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:719-724 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The credential scanner treats the `&` in `>&` and `<&` redirections as a command separator, breaking recursive parsing of shell `-c` command lines.
  WHY: Credentials in commands such as `sh -c 2>&1 'curl -u deploy:mycustompwd https://a.b'` can remain unmasked; reviewers classify this as a blocker.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:560-581 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `command_shape()` treats the `&` in `>&` and `<&` redirections as a command separator instead of part of the redirection.
  WHY: This corrupts command shapes and pattern signatures; reviewers disagree on severity, with deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro rating it BLOCKER and minimax_minimax-m3 rating it MAJOR.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:516-526 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `_segment_shape()` can process a redirection marker instead of the command argument following a shell `-c` flag.
  WHY: The command argument may be emitted as a positional word or generic flag instead of an opaque command line, exposing credentials in the reported shape.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:493-531 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `_segment_shape()` does not consume a dash-prefixed credential value when a redirection marker separates it from its credential flag.
  WHY: The value can be emitted verbatim in the permission-prompt report and issue title.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:248 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The command-flag regexes do not recognize PowerShell’s case-insensitive `-C` and `-COMMAND` forms when attached to an argument.
  WHY: The nested credential parser can be skipped, leaving the password unmasked in the reported command shape.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:549-558 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_segment_credentials` does not recognize single-dash command flags with `=`-attached command values.
  WHY: Credentials within those attached command lines are not parsed recursively and can remain unmasked in the permission-prompt report.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:184-187, 256 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The URL userinfo regex can match past `?` or `#` when a query or fragment contains an `@`.
  WHY: A URL such as `https://example.com?email=test@example.com` can be rewritten with the wrong hostname, corrupting the endpoint and causing the command to be withheld from the report.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:305-338 | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: `_segment_flag_letters()` searches for wrapped commands in a range that includes wrapper flags.
  WHY: A wrapper flag such as `-u` in `sudo` might be misinterpreted as a command word, causing incorrect credential-masking rules to be applied or skipped.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:442-446 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The attached-command handling in `_segment_shape` lacks a `continue`, so the token is reprocessed by subsequent flag-processing branches.
  WHY: Redundant token processing may result in incorrect or overly-masked command output.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:258 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: Backtick command substitutions are not recognized as command boundaries.
  WHY: Credential commands inside command substitutions may not be parsed, leaving credentials unmasked in the reported example or command shape.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:516-526 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `_shell_command_line_words()` can consume option-like words before a quoted command line as part of the shell `-c` command line.
  WHY: The shape may collapse those words into a single `*`, and recursive parsing may miss a credential value.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:715-716 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The here-string target is parsed as a command line only when `_shell_runner_before(with_digits, 0, len(with_digits))` is true.
  WHY: A here-string following a shell flag may not be parsed as a command line if the segment accumulator has been cleared.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "a redirection between a shell's `-c` and its command line (`sh -c 2>/dev/null 'mysql -p…'`), or between a credential flag and its value (`mysql >out -p…`, `curl -u >out user:pw`), split the command, so the credential reached the example; fixed twin-first (AD-16)" (PR description, Finding #1 table)
  expected_change_site: workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py, _command_line_credentials()
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  EVIDENCE: The fix for AD-16 handles `>` and `<` redirections between flags and values in the credential scan, but does not handle `&` as part of `>&` / `<&` combined operators. The `set(token) & set("<>")` condition on line 720 rejects `&` tokens, so `2>&1 'curl -u deploy:mycustompwd ...'` still splits the command at `&`, breaking the `-c` → command-line chain that AD-16 was meant to preserve. The test at line 390 covers `sh -c 2>&1 'curl -u deploy:mycustompwd https://a.b'` but the test fixture expects successful masking while the code path does not produce it.
- requirement: Mask credentials in permission-prompt reports before they are posted, including behind wrapper commands and inside shell/su -c command lines.
  expected_change_site: .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py and workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The attached-quote form (`-c'...'`) and PowerShell case-insensitive command-flag forms remain unparsed, allowing credentials to leak in reports, as identified by multiple reviewer models. The implementation diverges from the plan's stated goal of covering all `-c` command-line forms.
- requirement: The progress log must reflect the current state of the project (specifically that the twin sync has landed) so the conformance chain is not held on a stale BLOCKED status.
  expected_change_site: docs/implement-plan/issue-5124-mask-credentials-in-prompt-reports.md lines 7-14
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  EVIDENCE: The log continues to report Status: BLOCKED and lists the operator's twin-sync as the waiting-on condition, even though the sync has completed. This misrepresentation keeps the automated project advancement halted.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:719-724 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The `&` token in a split `>` + `&` redirection sequence is treated as a command separator, preventing recursive parsing of the nested command and leaving credentials unmasked.
  WHY: The nested `curl -u deploy:mycustompwd` command is not collected by `_command_line_credentials()`.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:720-723, `command_shape()` at lines 562-581 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_command_line_credentials()` and `command_shape()` treat `&` after `>` as a command separator; the shape can omit or misplace the command text after the redirection.
  WHY: The command payload can be omitted from the shape, corrupting pattern signatures while the credential scan fails to mask the credential.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:720-723 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The redirection-operator condition excludes `&`, so `>&` and `<&` are not recognized as redirection operators and the segment is split prematurely.
  WHY: Credentials within the `-c` command line are not collected, and the shape fallback can also be incorrect.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:516-526 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_segment_shape()` can pop a `\x00`-prefixed redirection token while handling a shell command flag, consuming none of the actual command line.
  WHY: The shape no longer reflects the shell command line as one opaque value, corrupting signature grouping.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:527 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A redirection token between a credential flag and a dash-prefixed credential value prevents credential-value consumption, so the value is emitted verbatim in the shape.
  WHY: The shape can expose the credential in issue titles, pattern-signature lines, and withheld-command notices.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:721 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The redirection-operator branch does not `continue` after setting `redirect`, leaving the control flow fragile and allowing `with_digits` tracking to persist through the operator.
  WHY: The reviewer states this is not a defect today but may affect future changes.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:723 | 
  PROBLEM: The redirection-operator branch does not extend a `>` or `<` redirection to include a following `&` token.
  WHY: The suggested minimal fix is to recognize the `&` token in the redirect context so it is not treated as punctuation.

=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:248 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The command-flag regexes do not correctly recognize PowerShell’s case-insensitive `-C` and `-COMMAND` forms when attached to an argument.
  WHY: The nested credential parser can be skipped, leaving the password unmasked in the reported command shape.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:549-558 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `_segment_credentials` does not recognize single-dash command flags with `=`-attached command values.
  WHY: Credentials within those attached command lines are not parsed recursively and can remain unmasked in the permission-prompt report.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:184-187, 256 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The URL userinfo regex can match past `?` or `#` and corrupt valid URLs lacking a trailing path slash when the query or fragment contains an `@`.
  WHY: A URL such as https://example.com?email=test@example.com can be rewritten as https://***@example.com, losing the hostname and corrupting the endpoint, causing the command to be withheld from the report.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:305-338 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `_segment_flag_letters()` searches for wrapped commands in a range that includes wrapper flags rather than just the wrapped command itself.
  WHY: A wrapper's own flag might be misinterpreted as a command word, leading to incorrect credential-masking rules being applied or skipped.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:442-446 | severity=HIGH | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The attached-command handling lacks a `continue` statement, so the token is reprocessed by subsequent flag-processing branches.
  WHY: This may result in incorrect or overly-masked command output.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:258 | severity=CRITICAL | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Backtick command substitutions are not r
